result.title: Recomputable tree encoder: store content, derive every vector (the embedding plane of the memory pyramid)
result.core_idea: Treat the memory plane's embeddings as a materialized view rather than as state. Only three things are stored as truth: each item's verbatim text, the structure (an append-only log of create, attach, merge, split, collapse, link and delete ops) and a versioned weight bundle. Every vector above the frozen leaf encoding is a pure function of (current content, current structure, weight version): leaf keys, a node's slot vectors, its sibling-aware vector and its gist vector. Each one is cached under a Merkle key and recomputed when its inputs change. The "small encoders between nodes" are shared inductive functions in the GraphSAGE style: an attention-pooling aggregator that encodes a node from its children, a sibling layer that makes it cross-contextual, a router conditioned on the query, and a structure scorer. So a node created a second ago gets a vector without retraining, and a deleted item's influence is gone once its ancestors are recomputed. Training never chases moving embeddings, because no trained parameter belongs to a single node. Gradients update only the shared functions, offline, on public or synthetic histories replayed as event streams into snapshots. On the phone, "learning" means forward recomputation plus explicit memory rows that can be deleted. A parent's relevance comes from an exact late-pooled score: the log-sum-exp of its leaves' scores, which does not depend on how the tree is shaped. Learned parts are only residuals on top of it. This fixes the measured failure of early mean pooling (0.386) and keeps the rule that weights rank but never hide.
result.representation:
Notation: d = 384 (the bge-small space), K = 4 slots, r = 16 head rank, E0 = frozen encoder, C(v) = children of v, L(v) = leaves under v, m = fan-out (at most 24 under the split rule), D = depth (about 5).

STORED (the source of truth, never learned):
- Leaf l: verbatim text t_l, source, time, taint, and a content hash h_l = H(t_l || taint).
- Structure, per axis (time, topic, entity, source): child lists and lateral links, kept as an append-only op log of create, attach, merge, split, collapse, link and delete. Each row holds ids, the op scorer's probability and the model version. The log holds no text.
- Gists g_v: text from the gist writer with a cite on every sentence. Each gist is tagged with the writer's version and with the Merkle hash of the children it was written from.
- The weight bundle W = (enc_ver, theta_ver): E0 plus every learned head, shipped and versioned together. Spaces are never mixed.
- Explicit personal rows, which can be inspected and deleted and carry provenance on every row:
  - alias rows (node v, ask leaf a), created only from answers whose cites passed the check;
  - P3b router pair counts, stored per source event;
  - read-ledger events.

FROZEN-MODEL CONTENT VECTORS (computed once per text, cached, kept because recomputing them needs E0):
- x_l = E0(t_l) for each leaf, y_v = E0(g_v) for each gist, and x_a for each ask leaf.
- Unit norm, int8 with one fixed global scale. There is no codebook trained on user data.
- Recomputed only when the encoder or the text changes.

LEARNED SHARED PARAMETERS (theta; trained off-device only; about 0.3M parameters besides E0):
- action head A(x) = norm(x + U_a V_a x) and state head S(x) = norm(x + U_s V_s x), the existing identity + rank-16 bridges;
- aggregator AGG, sibling layer SIB, router residual R, structure scorer O;
- level, axis and time embeddings, and 3 temperatures.
- Nothing anywhere is a free per-node embedding.

DERIVED VECTORS (a cache; a row is fresh only if its key (h_v, theta_ver, enc_ver, policy) matches the current one):
- Leaf key k_l = A(x_l).
- Node slots Z_v in R^{K x d} = AGG({u_j : j in C(v)}, y_v), with u_j = k_j for a leaf child and zbar_j for an internal child. This is recursive: the whole pyramid is one forward pass shaped like the tree, so the memory plane is itself an encoder, frozen at the leaves and learned above them.
- Pooled zbar_v = norm(sum_k Z_v[k]).
- Sibling-aware c_v = SIB(zbar_v, {zbar_u : u a sibling of v}): what v holds that its siblings do not.
- Exact statistics: leaf count n_v, time span, entity set, and a cone bound (centroid and angular radius of the descendant keys).
- Merkle hash h_v = H(sorted child hashes || H(g_v)).

COMPUTED PER QUERY, NEVER STORED:
- State s = S(x_q). Leaf scores sigma_l = s . k_l.
- Late-pooled node score rho_v = tau * log sum_{l in L(v)} exp(sigma_l / tau) - beta * tau * log n_v.
- Log-sum-exp is associative, so it is computed recursively over children. It depends only on the set of leaves under v, not on how they are grouped, so merges and splits cannot corrupt it.

POLICY VIEWS:
- A node with walled descendants keeps two derived rows, lab and strict. The strict row is computed only from children visible under strict, the same rule as MemoryPyramid's residuals, so a similarity score cannot reveal a walled leaf.

SIZE (N = 100k leaves, about M = 20k nodes):
- x and k in int8: about 77 MB. Z and c in int8: about 38 MB. About 115 MB in total, memory-mapped and excluded from backups.
result.internode_encoders:
1. AGG, child to parent (the "up" encoder).
- What it is: one multi-head attention-pooling layer with K learned seed queries (Set Transformer's PMA). It has no self-attention among children, so it stays sum-decomposable.
- Input per child j: u_j in R^384, plus phi(t_j) (a cosine time encoding of the child's time relative to the node's span, as in TGN), plus a level and axis embedding.
- For seed k (attention dimension d' = 64, 2 heads):
  - alpha_kj = softmax_j(q_k^T W_K [u_j; phi_j] / sqrt(d'))
  - P_v[k] = sum_j alpha_kj W_V u_j
  - Z_v[k] = norm(LN(q_k + W_O P_v[k]) + MLP(.) + gamma * W_G y_v)
  - When a gist is pending, a learned null token stands in for y_v.
- Output: K slots in the same 384-d key space as leaves, so one state vector s scores leaves and nodes with plain dot products. The node-unit score is max_k s . Z_v[k].
- Why slots: a session or a month holds several topics. One mean vector blurs them (the measured 0.386); a max over slots can match any one of them.
- Updates: the numerator sum_j exp(.) W_V u_j and the denominator sum_j exp(.) allow an O(K d') insert. A deletion always recomputes from the remaining children and never subtracts.
- Sharing: one AGG for every node, level and axis. About 150k parameters.

2. SIB, siblings to node (the "across" encoder).
- One cross-attention from zbar_v to its siblings: c_v = norm(zbar_v - lambda * Attn(zbar_v, {zbar_u}_{u != v})), with lambda learned in [0, 1].
- It is the vector form of the pyramid's residual lines: what is true of this child and not of its siblings.
- Cost O(m^2 d') per sibling set, with m at most 24. Shared, about 50k parameters.

3. R, the router conditioned on the query (the "between" decision when reading).
- For a parent p and a child v: r(s, v) = rho_v + rho_v^BM25 (normalized) + w^T MLP([max_k s.Z_v[k], s.c_v, rho_v, rho_v^BM25, log n_v, recency rank among siblings, level, alias score]).
- The last layer starts at zero, so on day one r equals the exact late-pooled plus lexical score. It learns only the residual (the P3b lesson).
- About 2k parameters. Output: an order over the children, and a calibrated probability that a child holds evidence, which drives the rule "jump straight there when sure".

4. O, the structure scorer (the "between" decision when writing).
- Pair head on (u, v): features [c_u * c_v elementwise, |c_u - c_v|, cone overlap, entity Jaccard, time gap, log sizes, same-parent flag] -> softmax over {none, link:entity, link:topic, link:time, merge}.
- Split head on v: features of a 2-means partition of its children (inertia ratio, slot spread, fan-out) -> P(split).
- Placement head for a new leaf: softmax over the top-m candidate holders by k_l . c_v.
- About 20k parameters. Its outputs are proposals only. A rule layer decides: split above 24 children, merge only into at most 12, hysteresis, at most 3 ops a night. Every decision is logged with its features, probability and theta_ver, so it can be inspected and undone.

5. Lateral step (not learned at first).
- At read time, one personalized-PageRank step from the top nodes over lateral links (HippoRAG).
- Later, one learned scalar per link type, a minimal form of HAGE's learned edge weights. Edge feature vectors only if scalars fail.

Sharing and the gist writer:
- All of theta is shared across nodes, levels, axes and users. Anything per node is either an exact statistic or an explicit row.
- The gist writer is an LLM: Claude on public data during training, the on-device model for private nodes. It is not an embedding module; its output enters only through y_v and the pack text.
result.dynamic_ops:
The same mechanism for every op:
- The op is first written as a structure-log row, then the hashes on its Merkle path are marked dirty, then derived rows are recomputed lazily.
- A read recomputes any stale node it touches, bottom-up (at most D*m child reads). The night pass flushes the rest.
- Nothing is updated by subtraction or by moving a stored vector.
- Cost symbols: e = one E0 pass (a few ms on the Neural Engine, to be measured), d' = 64, K = 4.

CREATE (a new leaf)
- One E0 pass (e). k = A(x) at O(d r). Append to the flat key matrix and the full-text (FTS5) index.
- Placement: the time axis by rule; topic and entity by O's placement head over the top-m holders (O(m d)).
- Dirty the ancestors on each axis (O(D) hashes). Recompute the parent's slots incrementally (O(K d')), each ancestor (O(m K d')) and the touched sibling sets (O(D m^2 d')).
- Total: one encoder pass plus under 1 ms. Log-sum-exp scores need no update because they are computed per query.

MERGE (u, w -> v)
- Log {u, w -> v, both child lists}.
- Compute Z_v by AGG over C(u) and C(w) from scratch, never as an average of Z_u and Z_w. Cost O((|C_u| + |C_w|) K d').
- Tombstone the old ids with a pointer to v. v's gist is pending (the null token) until the night rewrite, then one E0 pass.
- The ancestors and v's new sibling set go stale.
- Undo: apply the inverse op from the logged child lists; the vectors re-derive.

SPLIT (v -> v1, v2)
- 2-means over the children's c_j (O(m d) per iteration), or O's partition.
- Compute Z_v1 and Z_v2 from scratch. No Net2Net copying is needed, because nodes have no parameters to initialise. The log-sum-exp scores of the halves combine exactly into v's.
- Both gists pending.

COLLAPSE (v has one child left)
- Drop v's rows, attach the child to v's parent, recompute that parent and its sibling set.

REWRITE (a new gist for v)
- One E0 pass for y_v, recompute Z_v. h_v changes, so every ancestor goes stale.
- Cost: e plus O(D m K d').

FORGET (soft, for relevance)
- No vector changes. The item is flagged archived and kept out of default packs. Reversible, and still deletable.

DELETE (privacy, hard; synchronous, one transaction)
1. Remove:
   - t_l, x_l and k_l: overwrite the row, then compact;
   - its full-text postings and lateral links;
   - alias rows that point at l, or that were created by l if l was an ask;
   - read-ledger rows that cite l;
   - the P3b pair counts it contributed (counts are kept per event, so they subtract exactly; weights are re-derived from counts).
2. For every ancestor on every axis:
   - drop l from the child list;
   - discard the whole gist, not only sentences that cite l, because the writer read l when it wrote every sentence. Ancestors higher up were written from gists that held l, so their gists go too;
   - rewrite each discarded gist from the remaining children, and show totals and cites only until the rewrite lands;
   - recompute Z and c from scratch from the remaining children.
   A node left with no children was derived only from l and is deleted, recursively. A node left with one child collapses.
3. Structure-log rows that name l are redacted to a tombstone. Undo skips them, so an undo can never bring content back.
4. Storage:
   - SQLite secure_delete=ON, then a WAL checkpoint(TRUNCATE) and incremental_vacuum;
   - no HNSW, because its tombstones and neighbour lists keep traces;
   - no product-quantization codebooks trained on user data;
   - in-memory caches dropped.
5. Weights: theta never saw private data, so there is nothing to unlearn in the weights. That is why v1 does no on-device gradient training.
- The guarantee: after a delete, every derived row equals a fresh build without l, with the same theta, children in canonical id order, and the canonical fp32 CPU path. A shadow rebuild in tests checks this.
- Cost: O(D m K d') plus about D gist rewrites per axis. The rewrites are the dominant cost.

MODEL-WEIGHT UPDATE (a new theta, same encoder)
- No encoder pass.
- Build new k = A(x) columns: about 2 d r N, or 1.2 GFLOP at N = 100k, around a second.
- Then the nodes bottom-up (about N K d' operations, seconds).
- Then flip a version pointer (blue/green). The old columns serve until the flip.
- Aliases re-derive, because they store x_a and not S(x_a). Text, structure and gists are untouched.

ENCODER UPDATE (a new E0)
- Always ships with a theta trained for it; the two spaces are never mixed.
- Re-encode N leaves and M gists, (N + M) * e: about 10 min for 120k texts at 5 ms each, to be measured before shipping.
- Runs as a background processing task while charging and resumes from a leaf-id watermark. The old index serves until the flip. Storage doubles during the migration.
- Backward-compatible training (BCT) is an option only if mixing ever becomes necessary.

REASONING-MODEL UPDATE (Claude to Qwen3-8B)
- Train only a new state head from the LLM's hidden state into the existing key space, in the style of CLM-8B. This is query-side only, the route Atlas showed avoids re-indexing.
- No memory recompute at all.
result.training:
There are three time scales, and gradients exist in only one of them.

(a) RELEASE TIME, OFF-DEVICE (Mac or GPU; public and synthetic data only)

Data:
- LoCoMo with chat-held-out folds, LongMemEval and MSC.
- Synthetic long histories generated from public persona seeds, with known evidence, topic and entity labels. The structure labels come free with synthetic data.
- Gists for the training trees are written by Claude, over public or synthetic text only.

Episodes, as event-stream replay:
- This borrows TGN's training protocol but not its recurrent per-node memory, because a recurrent state absorbs deleted events and can only be rebuilt by replaying all history.
- Stream a history in time order through the real write path (rules plus the current O) to build a forest.
- At random checkpoints t, freeze the snapshot G_t and sample asks whose evidence arrived by t.
- Every derived vector is a function of the snapshot alone, so each snapshot is an ordinary training example: precomputed E0 vectors -> heads -> AGG up the tree -> SIB -> scores. The frozen encoder never runs inside the loop.
- There is no backprop through time, and snapshots batch independently.
- This is the direct answer to "can we train while the embeddings change": we train the functions, and the changing embeddings are their outputs on changing inputs.

Structure augmentation (in the spirit of DropEdge), applied to each snapshot:
- random splits, merges, collapses and fan-out changes;
- 10 to 20% of leaves dropped;
- gists nulled with probability 0.3, or swapped with a sibling's gist with probability 0.1.
The aggregator therefore trains on the structures a policy might produce, including bad ones.

Losses: L = L_leaf + l1 L_node + l2 L_route + l3 L_gist + l4 L_struct + reg.
- L_leaf: the existing bidirectional InfoNCE between S(x_q) and A(x_l), with negatives from the same chat.
- L_node:
  - per level, a multi-positive InfoNCE over that level's nodes, with node score tau * LSE_k(s.Z_v[k] / tau);
  - positives are nodes that contain evidence, weighted by their share of it;
  - a level where more than 30% of nodes are positive is skipped (a year contains everything).
- L_route:
  - at each parent on the hindsight path to evidence, BCE over its children on r(s, v), with target "contains evidence";
  - hindsight supervises every reading decision directly, so reading needs no RL.
- L_gist:
  - compute zbar_v with the gist masked out, then InfoNCE so that it retrieves y_v among its siblings' gist vectors;
  - this teaches the aggregator what a summary of these children looks like, and keeps nodes with a pending gist usable.
- L_struct, credit for discrete ops by counterfactual rollout (learning to search, in the DAgger/LOLS family):
  - at sampled states, list the candidate ops: the top merge pairs, splits of over-full nodes, link candidates, placement holders;
  - apply each one on a copy. Recompute is local to the touched path, so this is cheap;
  - replay the episode's next H asks and score J = recall@10 - lambda * pack tokens - mu * ops;
  - label the op with the best change in J, or "none" if no op beats a margin;
  - train O by cross-entropy on these labels plus the synthetic topic and entity labels.
- reg: the existing identity-proximity penalty ||U V||^2, weight decay, zero-initialised residual layers, clamped temperatures.

Alternation:
- Retrain AGG and R on structures produced by the new O, mixed 50/50 with structures from older policies, so the model does not chase its own tail.
- DiffPool-style soft assignment was considered and rejected: training and inference disagree once it is made hard.
- REINFORCE (HAGE's route) is kept only as a late fine-tune if rollouts plateau.

Stability:
- Frozen E0.
- Identity + rank-16 heads (full rank overfit, at 0.610).
- Zero-initialised router residual, so a new model starts at the exact baseline.
- EMA weights; 5-fold validation with whole chats held out.

Promotion gate for shipping a theta_ver. On held-out chats it must:
1. never lose recall to the exact floor (flat hybrid with log-sum-exp parents);
2. beat the current theta;
3. lose at most 0.01 on the perturbation suite (splits, merges and deletes at test time, with no retraining);
4. pass the checks that a recompute equals a rebuild and that a deleted item looks as if it never existed.

(b) NIGHT, ON DEVICE (no gradients)
- Structural ops from O plus the rules: at most 3 a night, with hysteresis, every one logged and undoable.
- Gist rewrites, a flush of stale rows, decay of counters, pruning of P3b pairs.

(c) EACH ASK, ON DEVICE (no gradients)
- Alias rows come only from answers whose cites passed the check. E6 showed that moving keys loses 0.023 under noisy or self-generated cites, so keys never move.
- Aliases are additive, capped at 8 per node, scored as max(k_v.s, max_a S(x_a).s - margin), decay over time, and are deleted by provenance.
- Personal learning lives in memory rows, not in weights. If an on-device adapter is ever added, it uses SISA-style time shards so a deletion retrains only its own shard.
result.inference:
READ (an ask becomes a pack for the reasoning plane), with N leaves and M nodes:
1. Normalize the ask (dates resolved by the P3b normalizer). x_q = E0(q), one pass. s = S(x_q). With an open reasoning model, s may instead come from a CLM-style state head on its hidden state.
2. Score every leaf: sigma = K s over the int8 key matrix, O(N d), about 38M operations at 100k (a few ms with Accelerate).
   - BM25 through FTS5, fused into one leaf ranking by RRF (k = 60).
   - This ranking is never gated: its top 10 leaves are always eligible for the pack. Weights rank; they never hide.
3. Tree pass, bottom-up over the live forest in the current policy view:
   - rho_v by segmented log-sum-exp over children, O(N + M);
   - node-unit score max_k s.Z_v[k], and s.c_v, O(M K d);
   - the node's BM25 score, the router's r(s, v), and alias scores (at most 8 per node).
4. Lateral step: one PageRank step from the top 5 nodes over entity, time and topic links.
5. Pack selection decides granularity, which is the reason the pyramid exists at all:
   - candidates are the top leaves plus the top nodes;
   - a node's gist replaces the leaves it covers when it covers at least c of the top leaves, or when its r is high while its children score diffusely. Otherwise leaves go in word for word;
   - a greedy knapsack under the token budget, never including both a node and its descendant;
   - every item carries its path and its cite ids;
   - a zoom request from the LLM reuses the same scores to open a node's children, with no recompute.
6. A pack node whose cache key is stale is recomputed before it is used, at most D*m child reads.

Read cost: one E0 pass plus O(N d + M K d) dot products plus sorting. About 10 to 30 ms at N = 100k, not counting the LLM. The keys are memory-mapped (about 115 MB).

WRITE (a new item):
1. Taint it, store the text as an op-log row, compute x = E0(t) and k = A(x), and append to the key matrix and FTS5. O(e + d r).
2. Place it on each axis: time by rule; topic and entity by O's placement head over the top-m holders.
   - Link proposals come from the pair head against the top-m nodes, O(m d). Attaches and links apply at once; merges and splits wait for the night.
3. Mark the ancestor paths dirty in the Merkle tree. They recompute lazily, O(D m K d') when touched.

Write cost: one encoder pass plus under 1 ms.

NIGHT:
- At most 3 structural ops.
- Gist rewrites for dirty nodes, bottom-up. The LLM is the dominant cost.
- E0 on the new gists, then a flush of all stale rows.
- Decay of counters and aliases.
- Sampled self-checks that a recompute equals a rebuild.

MODEL SWAP:
- Build the new derived columns in the background, then flip the version atomically. One ranking never mixes two versions.

PRIVACY DELETE:
- Synchronous and runs before any later read, at O(D m K d') plus the gist rewrites. Until a rewrite lands, the node shows totals and cites only.
risks: The learned parent vectors (AGG slots) may add nothing over exact log-sum-exp plus BM25 at LoCoMo's scale (about 600 turns and about 25 sessions per chat), where much of the evidence is lexical (names, dates). If so, AGG is overhead: parents should be scored by log-sum-exp plus BM25, and learning should be kept to the router residual and the structure scorer.

Too little training data. Ten LoCoMo chats, eight per fold, give about 200 sessions, and full-rank heads already overfit (0.610). The aggregator and the op scorer will lean on synthetic LLM-written histories, whose distribution differs from his notes, app records and turns, so gains may not transfer.

Counterfactual rollout labels for structural ops are only as good as the replayed asks. On public data those are benchmark questions, so O may learn structures that suit LoCoMo's question style rather than his.

The structure policy and the aggregator adapt to each other. Alternating training can oscillate, and the structures the phone actually produces (years deep, unusual fan-outs) may fall outside the augmentation range.

Recompute storms. The sibling layer makes a change non-local (every sibling's c_v), and a gist rewrite near the root stales wide sets. Lazy reads need a work budget. Only staleness that is not about privacy may be served with a flag; a deletion must always finish synchronously.

Deletion leaks outside the vectors: gist text written by a model that read the deleted item (hence the rule to rewrite whole gists along every ancestor path, costing about D LLM calls per axis), Spotlight and App Intents indexes, logs, crash reports, backups, and P3b router keys that are ask words. Any derived artifact without provenance breaks the guarantee.

Numerical determinism. Neural Engine fp16 and CPU fp32 give different floats, so 'recompute equals rebuild' holds bit for bit only on the canonical CPU path. On the Neural Engine, ties can flip in rankings. The honest guarantee is about inputs (no deleted input remains), not about bits.

An encoder upgrade on the phone costs minutes of Neural Engine time, battery and double storage. If a head is ever applied to the wrong encoder's space, retrieval degrades silently, so the bundle version check must refuse a mismatch.

The size correction beta in log-sum-exp pooling needs tuning: at beta = 0 big nodes always win, and at beta = 1 tiny nodes do. A wrong beta makes the late-pooled baseline, and so everything built on it, biased.
A gist that replaces leaves in the pack can lose the exact sentence the LLM needed. Top leaves stay verbatim, which costs tokens, and the pack rule needs its own answer-level evaluation.

Policy views double the derived rows. A bug that pools a walled child into the strict view would leak membership through similarity, so the strict view needs the same 'never there' tests MemoryPyramid has.

Recall@10 of evidence turns on LoCoMo does not measure what nodes are for (gist usefulness, pack efficiency, multi-hop context). The design can pass the retrieval test and still not help answers; it needs the P1b answer-level score as well.

Feeding node vectors into Qwen as soft memory tokens (projecting Z into its embedding space) would make the memory impossible to inspect. It is kept out of v1, and text stays the interface between the planes.
prior_work_used: GraphSAGE (Hamilton et al. 2017): shared inductive aggregators, so an unseen node gets an embedding without retraining. This is the reason no node has its own trained parameters.
Set Transformer, PMA attention pooling with learned seeds (Lee et al. 2019): the multi-slot child-to-parent aggregator, restricted to its sum-decomposable one-layer form.
ColBERT late interaction and MaxSim (Khattab and Zaharia 2020): score first, pool after. This motivates log-sum-exp parent scores over the early mean pooling that measured 0.386.

Temporal Graph Networks (Rossi et al. 2020): chronological event-stream replay, prequential evaluation and cosine time encodings are borrowed. Its recurrent per-node memory is rejected because it absorbs deleted events and needs full replay after a model update.
RAPTOR (Sarthi et al. 2024): a tree of LLM summaries embedded in the same space as the leaves. Here a gist enters as y_v = E0(g_v).
HippoRAG (Gutierrez et al. 2024): a personalized-PageRank step over lateral entity links at read time.

REALM (Guu et al. 2020) and Atlas (Izacard et al. 2022): the cost of index staleness when the document encoder trains. Atlas's query-side-only option is the basis for freezing E0, keeping document-side heads cheap to re-derive, and swapping reasoning models by training a state head only.
CLM-8B: contrastive state and action heads on a frozen Qwen3-8B. These are the existing bridges, and the route for an open reasoning plane to reach the same key space.

Jev-Mem (UT Dallas, reported as arXiv 2609.23986, Sep 2026; figures from secondary sources and not verified): a light System-One controller for store, link and retrieve, with the LLM used only for final reasoning. It is the model for keeping all internode decisions in small heads.

HAGE (Jiang et al., arXiv 2605.09942, May 2026): routing conditioned on the query over relation-specific weighted edges trained with RL. Borrowed as per-link-type edge weights. Its RL is replaced by hindsight supervision plus counterfactual rollouts.
Merkle trees and incremental maintenance of materialized views in databases: hashes along the changed path decide exactly what is stale, and derived rows are recomputed lazily.
SISA training (Bourtoule et al. 2021): exact unlearning by sharding, reserved for any future on-device adapter. In v1 no private data ever reaches a gradient.
Backward-compatible training (BCT; Shen et al. 2020): an option for encoder upgrades only if old and new vectors ever have to coexist.
Net2Net (from the P4 simulation): no longer needed for splits, because nodes have no parameters to initialise.
DAgger and LOLS (learning to search): credit for discrete structural ops through counterfactual rollouts instead of REINFORCE.
DiffPool (Ying et al. 2018): considered for soft structural assignment and rejected, because training and inference disagree once assignments are made hard.
DropEdge (Rong et al. 2020): structure augmentation, so the aggregator is robust to whatever structure the policy produces.
Cone and ball trees for maximum inner-product search: exact upper bounds that allow lossless pruning once a flat scan stops being cheap.
SQLite secure_delete, WAL checkpoint and incremental vacuum: physical removal of deleted rows.

The project's own results (docs/ai/harness/memory-pyramid.md, scripts/ai/small_models/e1, e5 and e6): weights rank but never hide (P4); learn only the residual (P3b); keys must not move under noisy cites, which favours alias rows (E6); identity + rank-16 heads (E5).
result.minimal_experiment:
The claim being tested: a parent node's representation should be computed from its children by a shared function, not stored. Such a representation should beat mean pooling (0.386), match or beat BM25 session choice (0.649), survive structural change at test time without retraining, and after a deletion be identical to a build that never held the item.

Setup:
- One CPU script, proposed as scripts/ai/small_models/e8_node_views.py.
- Reuse load() and train(rank=16) from e5_bridges.py and the pinned locomo10.json (its sha256 is checked).
- Same 5 folds, 2 held-out chats each. Level-1 nodes are LoCoMo's sessions.
- Cache the frozen bge-small vectors to an npz file. Encoding about 5.9k turns and about 1.5k questions takes 1 to 3 minutes.

Arms. Each one opens nodes until it has opened B leaves, where B = 3 x the chat's median session length on the unperturbed structure. A leaf budget instead of a node count keeps splits fair. Inside, each runs the same hybrid read as the 0.649 arm, and reports recall@10.
- A0: mean of frozen turn vectors. Should reproduce 0.386.
- A1: BM25 over sessions. Should reproduce 0.649.
- A2: log-sum-exp late pooling over the bridged leaf scores. No new training. tau in {0.02, 0.05, 0.1} and beta in {0, 0.5, 1}, both picked on the training folds only.
- A3: the PMA aggregator (K = 4, d' = 64, about 75k parameters) over bridged child keys plus a time feature. Trained with the L_node InfoNCE on the 8 training chats for about 40 epochs. Node score: max over slots.
- A4: RRF of A2 and A3. A5: RRF of A1 and A4.
- Reference: flat bridged+hybrid with no gating, from e5.

Dynamics on the held-out chats, using the same trained weights and no retraining:
- P1: split every session into two contiguous halves.
- P2: merge adjacent session pairs.
- P3: delete 15% of leaves at random, including some evidence; a question whose evidence is all gone is dropped, and recall counts only the remaining evidence.
- P4: move 10% of leaves into wrong sessions.
- After each, recompute every node vector from its children and rerun all arms.

Exactness checks:
- (a) An incremental insert using the decomposable sums equals a from-scratch recompute, max absolute difference under 1e-5.
- (b) Deleting a leaf then recomputing equals building without it: bit-identical in fp32, with children sorted by id.
- (c) Time to re-derive every leaf key and node vector after swapping a fold's head weights. The expectation is under 1 s for about 6k leaves.

Pass lines, set before the run:
- (1) A2, A3 or A4 is at least 0.649, and A5 is at least 0.665 with a bootstrap 95% CI against A1 that excludes 0.
- (2) Under P1 to P3, the best learned arm loses no more than A1 loses plus 0.01. This is the inductive claim.
- (3) Check (b) shows zero difference.

How to read the results:
- A2 roughly equal to A3: learned slots are unnecessary at session level. Keep exact late pooling and spend learning on the router and the structure ops.
- Both below 0.60: embeddings should not gate at all. Parents only rerank, with BM25 gating.
- A3 well above A2 and robust under P1 to P3: the aggregator earns its place, and the next step is level 2 (weeks of sessions) and gists.

Runtime: about 2 min to encode, about 3 min of training across 5 folds (the bridges plus the aggregator, both tiny), about 3 min of evaluation across 5 structures x 7 arms. About 10 min in all on a laptop CPU.

Not tested here: gists (no LLM call), lateral links, learned structural ops, and timings on the phone.

result.title: Derived, not stored: an inductive message-passing pyramid over frozen leaf vectors
result.representation:
Notation:
- E is the frozen text encoder (bge-small-en-v1.5, d=384).
- r=16 (rank); each parent has m<=4 slots and at most F=32 children.
- Each axis is about 5 levels deep: leaf -> session/day -> week or topic -> month -> year/root.
- The time, topic and entity axes are separate trees over the same leaves. A leaf has one parent per axis, plus lateral links.
- LR(x) = x + U(Vx), with U (d x r) initialised to 0. This is the identity-plus-low-rank form that measured 0.657 against 0.610 for full rank.

FROZEN (never trained here; computed once):
- E itself.
- Per leaf: c_x = E(text_x), unit norm, cached at ingest.
- g_v = E(gist_v) for any node that has a written gist, and c_q = E(ask).
- Because E never trains, leaf vectors are never re-encoded when the learned parts change. That alone answers the REALM/Atlas index-staleness problem: the costly encoder is fixed, and only light heads over cached vectors move (Atlas's query-side fine-tuning idea, pushed further).
- Exact side data, not learned:
  - the text, which is the source of truth;
  - timestamp, source, taint (privacy label) and BM25 postings;
  - each node's counts and time span;
  - a Merkle hash h_v = H(sorted child hashes, H(gist text), level, W_version, E_version).
- tau_x = phi(t_x) in R^16: fixed Fourier features of time (hour, weekday, log age, session ordinal).

LEARNED (global and shared: one copy for every node, axis and user):
- Trained offline only on public or synthetic data, shipped as a versioned blob W_k of about 0.55M parameters.
- Contents:
  - bridge heads S (ask state) and A (node action), identity + rank-16 as in E5;
  - up-encoder U;
  - lateral encoder L (4 relation types);
  - down encoder D (a GRU cell, a small gated recurrent network);
  - leaf contextualiser G;
  - op heads for attach, merge and split;
  - optional event GRU omega.
- Encoders are conditioned on a level embedding (FiLM, a learned per-level scale and shift) and on relation type, never on node id.
- No node has trainable parameters of its own. That is GraphSAGE's inductive property: nodes can appear and vanish without retraining.
- It also matches the P3 simulation, where sharing per level is what made learning fast.

DERIVED (a cache: a pure function of the graph, the frozen vectors, W_k and last night's snapshot; recomputed, never optimised directly):
- Internal node v:
  - K_v in R^{m x d}: routing slots, a multi-vector key scored by max;
  - u_v in R^d: summary vector;
  - rho_v: sibling residual, meaning what is true of v and not of its siblings. It is the vector twin of the P1 text residuals;
  - ctx_v: lateral context;
  - d_v in R^128: down-context, computed at night only, from nightly snapshots u_bar.
- Leaf x:
  - a_x in R^d: its contextual retrieval key;
  - A(c_x): the context-free key, which is what E5 measured.
- Each cached vector stores the hash it was computed under, and is valid only while that hash matches.

EVENT-SOURCED PERSONAL STATE (optional; the only place feedback lives):
- Per node, an event list of (ask-leaf id, node id, type in {verified cite, opened-not-cited, corrected}, time).
- m_v in R^64 is a fold of GRU_omega over those events, used only as a capped alias key.
- Since it can be rebuilt from the log, it can be undone, inspected, unlearned by replay, and re-derived under new weights.

TEXT SIDE stays text:
- Verbatim leaves and LLM-written gists with cites (P1b).
- Vectors decide where to look; text is what is shown, cited and deleted.
- Lab and strict policies get separate derived caches, so a walled leaf never enters a strict vector. This mirrors the separate lab and strict gists.
result.internode_encoders:
All of these are tiny shared modules: attention or GRU blocks of about 10k-250k parameters each, not LLMs, because they run on every write and are re-run in full on every weight release. Small LLMs appear only on the text side (described at the end).

Evaluation order is a DAG (directed graph with no cycles), so one sweep is enough:
content -> up -> lateral -> down -> leaf keys.

The up pass reads leaf CONTENT c_x, never the contextual keys a_x. That avoids a cycle, because a_x itself depends on the parent.

(1) Up-encoder U (children -> parent). Runs bottom-up on every internal node.
- Input: the set X = {x_c}, where x_c = c_c + P*tau_c for a leaf child and x_c = u_c for an internal child.
- Seeds: Z0_v = kmeans_m(X).
  - Deterministic: farthest-point initialisation from the child nearest the mean, 3 Lloyd iterations, ties broken by id.
  - m = min(4, |X|).
  - These seeds are derived per node, not learned.
- Slots: K_v = normalise(Z0_v + gamma_l * MHA_r(Q=Z0_v, K=X, V=X)).
  - MHA_r is 4-head attention with low-rank projections.
  - gamma_l in R^d is a per-level gate initialised to 0.
- Summary: u_v = normalise(LR_u(mean_j K_v[j]) + lambda_g * g_v). lambda_g is learned and is 0 when there is no gist.
- Outputs: K_v (routing slots) and u_v (summary).
- It accepts any number of children, gives the same result in any order, and never sees a node id.
- At initialisation it reduces to per-node k-means multi-centroid keys, a non-learned baseline that should already fix most of the mean-pooling collapse.

(2) Lateral encoder L (siblings and lateral links). One round of message passing.
- Relation types: sibling, same-entity, same-topic, adjacent-in-time.
- At most 8 neighbours per relation type, so the inputs to each node stay bounded.
- ctx_v = sum_r sum_{w in N_r(v)} beta^r_vw * W^V_r u_w
- beta^r_v. = softmax_w(<W^Q_r u_v, W^K_r u_w>/sqrt(d) + b_r(dt_vw)), where b_r is a learned bias on the time gap.
- All W are low-rank. Each relation type has its own weights, shared across all nodes (R-GCN/GAT style).
- Sibling residual: rho_v = u_v - sum_{w in sib(v)} softmax_w(<u_v,u_w>/T) * u_w. This gives siblings the "cross-contextual" awareness the owner asked for.

(3) Down encoder D (parent -> children context). Internal nodes only; nightly.
- d_root = 0
- d_v = GRUCell_D(input=[u_bar_v ; ctx_v], hidden=d_parent(v))
- It reads nightly snapshots u_bar, so a daytime write never sends an update down the whole tree.

(4) Leaf contextualiser G (gives each leaf its retrieval key, the "action" side of the bridge).
- a_x = normalise(A(c_x + g * LR_G([c_x ; u_p(x) ; ctx_x ; tau_x ; d_p(x)]))), where g in R^d is initialised to 0.
- At initialisation a_x = A(c_x), exactly E5's low-rank bridged key (0.657). Training can only add context on top: who is speaking, which session and when, what the session is about, and what sets this turn apart from its neighbours.
- Each leaf's inputs are limited to its parent and its lateral neighbours. That limit is also the limit on how far a write invalidates cached vectors.

(5) Bridge heads (reasoning plane <-> memory plane).
- Today: s_q = normalise(S(E(q))).
- Later, with an open reasoning model: s_q = normalise(S'(pool(h_Qwen3-8B(q)))), with S' trained on public data, as CLM-8B puts heads on a frozen Qwen3-8B.
- Scores:
  - leaf: <s_q, a_x>;
  - node routing: max_j <s_q, A(K_v[j])>;
  - node as a candidate in its own right (RAPTOR collapsed tree): <s_q, A(u_v)>.
- Claude gets text packs; soft-token injection is only possible with an open model, later.

(6) Op heads (small shared MLPs that only PROPOSE; rules and caps execute).
- attach(x,p) = MLP([A(c_x) ; u_p ; A(c_x)*u_p ; phi(t_x - t_p)])
- merge(v,w) = MLP([u_v+u_w ; |u_v-u_w| ; sizes ; co-cite rate ; lateral overlap]), symmetric in v and w
- split(v) = MLP([dispersion of X under A ; best 2-means gain ; |C(v)| ; slot entropy])

(7) Optional TGN-style memory. Default off until it beats E6's anchored rule under noisy cites.
- Update: m_v <- GRU_omega(m_v, [s_q ; type ; log dt]), applied only for verified cites.
- Alias score: <s_q, A(P m_v)> - margin, with ||P m_v - u_v|| <= cap.

Weight sharing: U, L, D, G, S, A and the op heads are each a single copy used by every node and every axis. They are conditioned only on level (FiLM gamma_l, beta_l) and relation type.

Text-side "small models between nodes": the gist writer reads child texts and child gists and writes a cited gist. It runs at night: the on-device Foundation Model for private nodes, Haiku for lab nodes, per P1b. Its output enters the embedding plane only through g_v = E(gist).
result.dynamic_ops:
Cost unit: one up-encoder call is about 0.8M multiply-adds (k-means 3x4x32x384 plus low-rank attention). One leaf key is about 45k multiply-adds.

Write-time invalidation covers:
- the item's own vectors;
- the ancestor path (D nodes);
- siblings' ctx and a (at most F=32);
- lateral neighbours (at most 8 per relation type).

Night-time invalidation covers:
- the snapshots u_bar and the down states d;
- the leaf keys under nodes whose d changed;
- gists and structural ops.

Exactness invariant, tested: cache == full_recompute(G_now, snapshot_lastnight).

Ops log: every structural op is an OpRecord holding only ids and partitions, so its inverse can be replayed. Undo needs no stored vectors, because every vector is derived.

CREATE LEAF x
- c_x = E(text). This is the one encoder pass, about 5-20 ms on the Neural Engine for a 64-token turn.
- Add x to BM25 and to the flat index.
- Attach per axis:
  - time: exact, to the open session or day;
  - topic: attach head over the top-8 candidate parents from nearest-neighbour search on u, with hysteresis;
  - entity: through the entity linker.
- Recompute the path and the siblings: about 4M + 1.5M multiply-adds, about 1-3 ms. No training.

CREATE INTERNAL NODE (new session, day or topic)
- K and u come from one forward pass over its children.
- Insert it into the hash tree and recompute the parent path. O(F*d*r + D*0.8M).

MERGE (v, w) -> z
- C(z) = C(v) union C(w), and K_z and u_z are computed fresh.
- Hysteresis: merge only when |C(z)| <= 12; split above F.
- z's gist is marked stale. Until the night rewrite, lambda_g=0, so the vector summary stands alone.
- Children's d and leaf keys are recomputed at night.
- Undo = split by the stored partition. It is exact, because the vectors are derived.
- Cost: O(|C(z)|*d*r) plus the path.

SPLIT v -> v1, v2
- Partition by deterministic 2-means on X (or by the split head).
- v1 and v2 inherit v's gist text until it is rewritten. This is the Net2Net-style continuity trick: both start from the parent's gist, so reads do not jump.
- The parent gains one child; recompute v1, v2 and the path.
- Undo = merge.

COLLAPSE v (one child, or below the minimum size)
- Re-parent its children to p(v), delete v, recompute the path of p(v).
- The log keeps v's child list and gist hash for undo.

REWRITE v (new gist text)
- One E pass gives g_v; recompute u_v and the path.
- Down-context for the subtree is recomputed at night.
- The old gist stays in the log for inspection and undo, unless a privacy deletion purges it.

FORGET x (privacy deletion; must be exact)
1. Delete text_x, c_x, a_x, x's BM25 postings and its nearest-neighbour index entry. Rebuild that index segment rather than leaving a tombstone. Also delete the events and read-ledger paths that name x.
2. Remove x from its parent in every axis. The hash tree marks its ancestors dirty. Recompute the up-paths, siblings and lateral neighbours immediately, not at night, because their caches mixed in c_x.
3. Gists:
   - delete every sentence that cites x;
   - any gist whose input set included x (every ancestor gist written since x arrived) is regenerated bottom-up from the remaining children;
   - until then lambda_g=0, so a gist that may paraphrase x is never embedded.
4. A node left with 0 children is deleted; a node left with 1 child collapses.
5. Replay m_v from the event log without x's events.
6. Purge undo payloads and old gists that contain x, leaving id-only tombstones. A privacy deletion cannot be undone, by design.
7. Storage: SQLite secure_delete on, incremental vacuum, and backups of derived caches excluded.
8. Shared weights W never saw private data, so x had no influence on them and there is nothing to unlearn there.

The invariant "all private influence lives in leaves, in derived caches, or in event-sourced state" is what makes deletion exact.
- Verify by recomputing from scratch on G without x: every hash and vector must match, and grep every store for x's rare tokens.
- Cost: a few milliseconds of vector work, plus up to D gist rewrites (the expensive part: seconds on device).

FORGET BY SALIENCE (not privacy)
- Never deletes. It lowers priors and decays aliases, and may move the leaf to cold storage, but the leaf stays in BM25 and the flat index: weights rank, they never hide.

WEIGHT UPDATE W_k -> W_k+1
- W_version is part of every hash, so every derived vector becomes invalid.
- c_x and g_v do not change (E is frozen), so no text is re-encoded.
- Re-derive into a shadow cache in the background:
  - for N = 200k leaves and I = 30k internal nodes: N*45k + I*0.8M, about 3.3e10 multiply-adds;
  - about 5-20 s on the phone CPU, under 5 s on the GPU or Neural Engine.
- Swap atomically; reads use W_k until the swap.
- m_v is re-folded from the event log under the new S and omega. The log stores ids only, and s_q is recomputed from c_ask.
- Any vector that was persisted outside the cache would be stale, so the rule is: never persist derived vectors anywhere else, only ids and paths.

ENCODER MIGRATION (E changes, for example to embeddinggemma)
- The only expensive op: re-encode every leaf and gist, N+I passes of about 4 GFLOP each.
  - For 200k leaves that is about 8e14 FLOP, minutes to tens of minutes on the Neural Engine, run overnight while charging.
- It also needs a newly trained W, because heads are tied to one encoder, as CLM notes.
- Rare, versioned and double-buffered.
result.training:
Principle: within a training step the structure is a fixed input, so gradients never chase a moving graph. Training always does a full recompute (it is cheap: about 600 leaves and 25-35 sessions per LoCoMo chat). Deployment recomputes incrementally. A property test asserts the two agree to 1e-5.

DATA (no private data, ever):
- LoCoMo: 10 chats, about 1,531 questions with evidence; licence CC BY-NC.
- LongMemEval: evidence sessions and turns are labelled.
- MSC.
- Synthetic personal-like streams written by a public LLM from templates:
  - planted facts that change over time, so the model learns about superseded facts;
  - entities that recur across sessions;
  - questions with evidence ids and the time each is asked.
  - The synthetic set also yields labels for structural ops.
- Cross-validation is grouped by conversation (as E5: 5 folds, never test on a chat seen in training). Cross-dataset tests: train on LoCoMo plus synthetic, test on LongMemEval, and the reverse.

EPISODE:
1. Sample a conversation and a cut time t*.
2. Replay the builder over events up to t* to get G_t*.
   - Time axis: exact sessions and days.
   - Topic axis: P4 rules on frozen vectors.
3. Apply structure augmentation:
   - merge adjacent sessions, p=0.3;
   - split sessions longer than 20 turns, p=0.3;
   - drop non-evidence leaves, p=0.1 (stands in for forgetting);
   - drop lateral edges, p=0.2.
4. Batch = the questions whose evidence is at or before t*.
5. Forward = a full sweep: content -> up -> lateral -> down -> leaf keys.
6. Build a second, independently augmented view G' of the same episode for the stability loss.
This is the TGN recipe of training over event streams. Truncation is natural: a step's gradient flows only through the snapshot at t*, never across earlier writes.

LOSSES:
- L_leaf: bidirectional multi-positive InfoNCE on <s_q, a_x>, exactly E5's loss but on contextual keys. Hard negatives: the evidence turn's neighbours in the same session.
- L_route: for each level l, a multi-positive softmax over the nodes of that level. Scores are max-slot, and positives are the ancestors of any evidence leaf.
  - Plus a coverage term: -log softmax of the LOWEST-ranked positive. Multi-hop questions need every evidence session, not just one.
  - Hard negatives: siblings of the evidence session.
- L_gist (only where a gist exists): 1 - cos(LR_p(u_v), g_v). This teaches the up-encoder to summarise into the same space the text gists live in, so a node with no gist yet still has a sensible stand-in.
- L_stab: sum over leaves untouched by either augmentation of ||a_x(G) - a_x(G')||^2, plus the same for routing scores of untouched nodes. A rank-preservation term in the spirit of consistency regularisation: an unrelated merge must not reshuffle the rest of memory.
- L_anchor: ||LR||_F^2, E5's "stay near identity" term, plus weight decay.
- Total: L = L_leaf + 0.5 L_route + 0.1 L_gist + 0.1 L_stab + 0.01 L_anchor.

CREDIT ASSIGNMENT FOR DISCRETE OPS, in three tiers. Ship tier A first.
- (A) Rule-driven ops: time axis exact; session and day boundaries; topic split, merge, collapse and settle per the P4 rules with hysteresis and at most 3 ops a night. Nothing needs credit. The encoders are trained to be robust to the distribution of structures these rules produce, widened by augmentation.
- (B) Attach (topic axis) is relaxed so it can be differentiated, like DiffPool.
  - During training a leaf's topic parent is a Gumbel-softmax over the top-k candidates, w_xp = softmax(attach(x,p)/T).
  - The parent's up-attention adds log w_xp to that child's logits, so the retrieval loss sends gradient into the attach head.
  - T is annealed from 1.0 to 0.1, with a straight-through hard forward pass in late epochs. At deploy: argmax plus a re-attach margin delta.
- (C) Merge, split and collapse use paired counterfactual rollouts in the simulator.
  - At a candidate op o at time t, fork G_t into G_t+o and G_t (no-op) and evaluate the loss on the next H sessions' questions with the current encoders.
  - Both arms are exact and cheap, because everything is derived.
  - Label y_o = 1[dL_o < -eps], weighted by |dL_o|, and fit the op head with weighted logistic loss. This is a contextual bandit where both arms are observed: no REINFORCE variance, no reward shaping.
  - No-op is the default. Act only when the predicted gain clears a margin.
  - On the phone, an executed op is reverted automatically if the next nights' verified-cite rate on that subtree drops. The read ledger stores paths only.
- Two timescales, alternating, like hard EM:
  - encoders get N gradient epochs under the current op policy;
  - then the op heads are refit on fresh paired rollouts with the frozen encoders;
  - the final encoder epochs run with the op heads frozen, so the encoders fit the structure distribution that will actually ship.
- Gist rewrites are not trained by RL. Text checks (cites, numbers) judge them, and L_gist couples them to the vectors.

STABILITY TRICKS:
- frozen E;
- zero-initialised gates (gamma_l, g, ReZero-style), so step 0 equals the measured 0.657 system with k-means slots, and training can only add on top of it;
- rank 16 rather than full rank (full rank measured 0.610 because of overfitting);
- deterministic k-means seeds;
- fanout cap F bounds attention size;
- temperatures learned but clamped; gradient clipping;
- EMA weights for release;
- curriculum: true sessions first, then the augmentation rate is raised.
- Release gate:
  - W_k+1 must beat W_k on held-out chats and on a fixed synthetic personal-like world, per question category;
  - it must pass the fp16 parity test: Neural Engine ranks must match fp32 top-10 on at least 99% of asks.

NO ON-DEVICE GRADIENT TRAINING of W:
- Personalisation lives only in event-sourced state: m_v and aliases, and the existing P3b router weights.
- If a personal adapter is ever needed: SISA-shard it by month and retrain a shard when it receives a deletion.

TESTING, i.e. how "dynamic embeddings" stay testable:
- Property tests:
  - incremental == full recompute;
  - permutation invariance;
  - undo round-trip gives identical hashes and vectors;
  - forget(x) equals a build without x;
  - privacy deletion leaves no trace (token grep).
- Benchmark protocol: streaming. Each question is answered on G_t at the time it is asked, against a flat baseline over the same leaves at the same t.
- Stability metric: Kendall tau of the ranks of untouched items before and after each op type.
result.inference:
READ PATH (ask q). Sizes assume N = 200k leaves, I = 30k internal nodes, D = 5 levels, F = 32, d = 384.
1. Encode the ask:
   - c_q = E(q), frozen, about 5-15 ms on the Neural Engine;
   - s_q = normalise(S(c_q)), about 12k multiply-adds.
   - Later, with Qwen3-8B as the reasoning model, s_q comes from S' on its hidden state.
2. Three candidate streams. None of them hides anything:
   - (a) BM25 over leaves: O(postings of the query terms).
   - (b) Flat dense search: <s_q, a_x> over all leaves, N*d = 77M multiply-adds, about 5-10 ms with Accelerate. Or an HNSW nearest-neighbour index at O(log N) once N passes about 1e6.
   - (c) Tree beam per axis: from the root, score children by max_j <s_q, A(K_c[j])> and keep a beam of B = 4 per level.
     - Cost O(axes * D * B * F * m * d), about 1M multiply-adds per axis.
     - It gives p(v|q) = softmax over siblings, chained down the path.
     - Internal nodes are also scored directly as candidates, <s_q, A(u_v)> (RAPTOR collapsed tree), so a gist can answer a broad ask.
3. Fuse. A leaf's score is RRF(BM25 rank, dense rank) + lambda * sum over ancestors v of log p(v|q).
   - This is p(leaf|q) proportional to p(session|q) * p(leaf|session,q), applied as a soft prior.
   - A leaf outside the beam takes the prior of its nearest scored ancestor, floored. It never gets minus infinity: weights rank, they never hide.
   - Optional: the capped alias score from m_v enters as max(base, alias - margin).
4. Pack for the reasoning plane under the token budget:
   - the top gist nodes (text) with their paths;
   - the top-k leaves verbatim with cites;
   - filtered by taint and policy (the Door, the existing gatekeeper for what leaves the device).
   - For Claude the pack is text only. With an open model later, soft tokens are an option.
5. Feedback: the answer's verified cites go to the event log as ids, type and time. Nothing else changes at read time.
- Total: about 20-40 ms on the phone, dominated by encoding the ask.
- Complexity: O(N*d) or O(log N) for dense search, plus O(D*B*F*m*d) for the tree, plus BM25.

WRITE PATH (new item x). Nothing in this path trains.
1. Taint and normalise, as in the input-hygiene plan. c_x = E(text), about 5-20 ms. Add x to BM25 and to the flat index.
2. Attach per axis:
   - time: exact (open session or day; create the node if none);
   - topic: attach head over the top-8 candidate parents from nearest-neighbour search on u, re-attaching only past a margin;
   - entity: through the linker.
   Log each attach as an op.
3. Hash tree: mark the D ancestors per axis dirty. Recompute K and u along each path, about D*0.8M multiply-adds.
4. Recompute ctx and a for x, its siblings (at most F) and its lateral neighbours (at most 8 per relation type), about 1.5M multiply-adds.
   - x's down-context is d of its parent from last night's snapshot, or 0 for a new parent.
- Total: about 1-3 ms of vector work plus one encoder pass. Memory: about 1.5 KB fp32 per vector (0.75 KB fp16). With 200k leaves and 30k nodes x 5 vectors, that is about 0.6 GB fp32 or 0.3 GB fp16. Storing a and K in int8 brings it to about 150 MB.

NIGHT PATH (charging):
1. Rewrite stale gists bottom-up (text side) and recompute g_v.
2. Take snapshots u_bar; recompute d for dirty subtrees and the leaf keys under them, with a budget of about 50k leaves, about 1 s.
3. Propose structural ops (rules first, op heads where enabled), execute at most 3 per axis, log each.
4. Fold the event-sourced memories.
5. Audit: fully recompute a random 1% sample against the cache, and check that every hash is consistent.
risks: At LoCoMo scale the tree may add nothing to recall. Each chat is about 600 turns, and flat search plus BM25 is cheap and already the best measured (0.657). Choosing sessions with BM25 first lost (0.649). The pyramid's justified value may be context for leaf keys and packing, not routing; the design keeps flat search as the floor so this risk costs tokens, not recall.

Overfitting on tiny supervision: 8 training chats per fold and about 1.5k noisy evidence labels. Even full-rank bridges overfit (0.610), and a GNN adds parameters. Zero-initialised gates and rank 16 bound the damage, but contextualisation may simply learn nothing. Synthetic data may help or may teach artefacts of the generator.

Distribution shift: LoCoMo and LongMemEval are scripted persona chats. Kaushik's memory is app records, short told lines and notes. Weights tuned on benchmark chats may route his data worse than k-means slots that learn nothing.

Train and deploy structures may diverge. Encoders fit the structures the rule builder produces; once learned ops change that distribution, encoder quality can drop (op heads and encoders adapting to each other). Alternating training and augmentation reduce this but do not remove it.
Over-smoothing: sibling and down context can make turns in one session look alike and hurt single-hop precision. Watch the per-category numbers. The gate may need to be per category or per ask type.

Incremental cache bugs: the down-context depends on last night's snapshot, and a missed dirty mark, an order-dependent k-means, or fp16 drift on the Neural Engine silently diverges from full recompute. Mitigated only by the property tests and the nightly audit sample.

Feedback loops: E6 measured -0.023 with 60% wrong cites or self-feedback. The event-sourced memory must use verified cites only and stay capped, and can still entrench early mistakes. It is default off until it beats E6's anchored rule under noisy cites.

Counterfactual op labels are weak. Most single merges or splits change future loss by less than noise, with few questions per conversation, so learned op heads may never beat the P4 rules. Rules stay the default.
Phone budget: a 5-year memory of derived caches (about 0.3-0.6 GB unquantised) plus a shadow copy during a weight swap. int8 quantisation is needed and may cost ranking quality.

Bridging to an LLM's hidden states (CLM-style on Qwen3-8B) needs a separately trained projector per backbone; with Claude there are no hidden states, so text is the only bridge and soft-token injection is out of reach.
Licence: LoCoMo is CC BY-NC. Fine for research on a personal app, but weights trained on it should not ship commercially without checking.
prior_work_used: GraphSAGE (Hamilton et al. 2017): aggregator functions learned once and shared by every node, so unseen nodes get embeddings without retraining. This is the core of 'derived, not stored'.

Temporal Graph Networks (Rossi et al. 2020): per-node memory updated by GRU messages on an event stream, trained over event streams with truncated backprop. Used for the optional event-sourced m_v and for episode construction.
Set Transformer, Pooling by Multihead Attention (Lee et al. 2019): order-invariant set pooling into m slots. The up-encoder uses it, seeded with per-node k-means centroids.
ColBERT multi-vector late interaction (max-sim): routing slots are scored by max because measured mean pooling collapses (0.386).
DiffPool (Ying et al. 2018) and Gumbel-softmax straight-through (Jang et al. 2017): differentiable relaxation of the discrete attach decision.
R-GCN / GAT: lateral attention with separate weights per relation type (sibling, entity, topic, time).
Tree-LSTM style up and down recurrences: separate bottom-up summary and top-down context passes.
RAPTOR (Sarthi et al. 2024): a tree of LLM summaries; its finding that collapsed-tree retrieval beats strict traversal is why internal nodes are scored as candidates and the tree never hides.
HippoRAG: lateral entity links and graph propagation as a second retrieval signal.
REALM and Atlas: index staleness when encoders train; Atlas's query-side-only fine-tuning motivates freezing E and making every learned part a light head over cached vectors.

CLM-8B (heads on a frozen Qwen3-8B with bidirectional InfoNCE; https://huggingface.co/sekkit/CLM-v0.1-8B, https://github.com/Contrastive-LM/CLM): the bridge-head recipe, already reproduced in E5 with bge-small.

Jev-Mem (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.23986): a System-One controller separated from System-Two reasoning. Supports doing structure decisions with small fast modules and keeping the LLM out of the write path.

HAGE (https://arxiv.org/pdf/2605.09942): RL over relation-weighted edges for query-conditioned traversal. Taken as a caution: paired counterfactual rollouts replace REINFORCE here because the graph is cheap to fork.
Net2Net (Chen et al. 2016): function-preserving growth. Split children inherit the parent's gist so reads do not jump.
Merkle trees and self-adjusting / incremental computation: hash-keyed caches so a change recomputes only its own path.
ReZero / zero-initialised residual gates and LoRA-style low rank: step 0 equals the measured baseline, and few parameters.
MoCo-style EMA weights and consistency regularisation: stable releases and invariance to unrelated structural edits.
SISA (Bourtoule et al. 2021) and event sourcing: exact unlearning by replay. Used only if on-device personal training is ever added.
This repo's own results: E1/E5/E6 (scripts/ai/small_models), the P3 shared-per-level and P4 grow/split/merge simulations, and the P1 hash staleness and residuals (docs/ai/harness/memory-pyramid.md).

result.title: Text is truth, vectors are activations: an inductive pyramid encoder with heap-distilled parent keys and learning-to-search structural ops
result.core_idea: Treat the whole memory plane as one small, shared-weight, hierarchical set encoder. Its input is the current graph, and its activations are the node vectors: node embeddings are cached activations, never per-node parameters. Leaves keep a frozen content embedding (bge-small) plus the existing low-rank bridge. Each parent's routing keys are computed by one shared attention-pooling aggregator from its children's keys and its gist embedding. That aggregator is trained without labels to reproduce the exact "best match anywhere below this node" flat-retrieval score (max-heap distillation), which targets the measured failure of mean-pooled parents (0.386). Because all weights are global and inductive, and every vector is a pure function of (current content, structure, weight version), a structural edit only reruns the aggregator along the Merkle-dirty path. A weight update rebuilds the derived caches without re-embedding any leaf, and a deletion becomes exact by recomputation. Training never backpropagates through a changing graph. For the retrieval nets the graph is an episode input, sampled from a randomized distribution of structures. The discrete structural ops are learned separately, by learning-to-search with one-step counterfactual rewards on synthetic and public event streams. Global weights never see private data, so a privacy deletion needs cache recomputation and an optional subtree replay, not model unlearning.
result.representation:
Notation: d = 384. E = the frozen bge-small-en-v1.5 encoder. v = the weights version (one id for the whole learned bundle). HMAC_k = a keyed hash whose key never leaves the device.

LEAF i (a verbatim item: chat turn, note, object event)
- Stored truth (inspectable): text t_i; metadata (timestamp, speaker/source, session id, extracted entity ids); BM25 postings.
- x_i = E(t_i) in R^384. A FROZEN function, cached under HMAC_k(t_i) plus the encoder version. Re-embedded only during an explicit encoder migration.
- a_i = normalize(x_i + U_a V_a^T x_i), the action/key head, identity plus rank 16. The weights are LEARNED globally; the vector is DERIVED per leaf and cached under (H_i, v).
- No free per-node parameters.
- Optional, off by default: a usage vector u_i, a clipped EMA of s(q_e) over explicitly confirmed cite events e. It is derived by a fixed rule from the on-device cite log and deleted together with that log.

INTERNAL NODE p at level l >= 1 (session, episode, topic, era)
- Stored truth (inspectable):
  - gist text G_p, written by the gist LLM;
  - provenance: the list of (child id, child hash) the gist was written from;
  - stats: count, time span, entity set.
- g_p = E(G_p). A FROZEN function of the gist text; a learned "absent" token stands in when there is no gist yet.
- K_p in R^{m_l x d}, the routing keys (m_1 = 4, m_>=2 = 8, capped by the number of inputs). DERIVED by the shared aggregator U_theta from the multiset of child keys (a_c for leaf children, the K_c rows for internal children) plus g_p.
- Routing score: r(q,p) = tau * log sum_j exp(<s(q), K_pj> / tau), with tau = 0.05 (a soft max over the keys).
- z_p in R^d, a summary state used by the lateral scorer and the op policy, not for routing. DERIVED: z_p = normalize(mean_j K_pj + W_g g_p).
- Lexical signature: summed term frequencies and length of all descendants. Exact and additive, so a deletion just subtracts.
- rho_p, the heap residual: the mean, over a fixed set of probe queries, of |r(q,p) - t(q,p)|, where t is the exact subtree score defined in training. DERIVED and label-free; used as a split signal and an on-device health metric.
- Merkle hash H_p = HMAC_k(level || hash(G_p) || sorted H_c over the children). Every derived vector of p is cached under (H_p, v). When that key is missing, the vector is recomputed. That is the entire staleness rule.

LATERAL EDGE (u,v)
- Type: topic, entity, temporal sequel, or update/contradiction.
- Support set: the leaf ids whose content justifies the edge.
- Raw features: time gap, shared entities, co-evidence count.
- Weight w_uv = L_phi(features, z_u, z_v), DERIVED and cached under (H_u, H_v, v).

QUERY SIDE
- x_q = E(q), FROZEN. s(q) = normalize(x_q + U_s V_s^T x_q), the existing rank-16 state head (LEARNED; this is the 0.657 bridge).
- Later, once the reasoning plane is an on-device open model, a second state head s'(q) = normalize(W h_LLM(q)) can map a mid-layer hidden state (CLM-8B style) into the same 384-d space. The memory index is anchored by the frozen leaf encoder, so changing the reasoning model only retrains a query-side head.

SUMMARY
- FROZEN: E, used for leaves, gists and queries.
- LEARNED: the bridge heads S and A, the placement head P, the aggregator theta, the lateral scorer phi and the op policy psi. They are global, trained only on public or synthetic data, and shipped as one versioned bundle of under 0.5M parameters.
- DERIVED: a_i, K_p, z_p, rho_p, w_uv and the lexical signatures. These are pure functions of current content, structure and v; they can always be recomputed and are never trained per node.

So node embeddings are the activations of one hierarchical set encoder, not its weights. That is why a changing structure is compatible with training, deletion and undo.
result.internode_encoders:
Every module below is shared by all nodes: one set of weights per module, like GraphSAGE's aggregator. A node created a second ago therefore gets its vectors without any retraining. All learned parts use low-rank, zero-initialised residuals: the full-rank bridge overfit (0.610 vs 0.657 low-rank).

1. Bridge heads (already exist). S maps the ask to a state; A maps a node to an action key. Identity plus rank 16, about 25k parameters. Input x in R^384; output a unit vector in the shared key space.

2. Placement head P. Identity plus rank 16 on x_new. It answers "where does this new item belong" with the same r(., p) the read path uses, so placement and retrieval live in one space. Output: the top-3 candidate parents with their scores.

3. Up-aggregator U_theta (child to parent), the core internodal encoder.
- Input: the set C_p of child keys (d-vectors). Each gets tags added through a rank-8 projection: level, the child's rank in time within p (sinusoidal), source type. The gist token g_p is appended, replaced by the learned "absent" vector when dropped.
- Step 1, baseline: B_p = a deterministic farthest-point selection of m rows from C_p, starting at the child nearest the set medoid, ties broken by id. This non-learned multi-vector baseline already avoids the mean collapse.
- Step 2, attention: H = MAB(Q = B_p, KV = C_p plus g_p). One multi-head attention block (4 heads, rank-32 Q/K/V projections, rank-32 FFN), in the style of the Set Transformer's PMA but with data-chosen seeds instead of fixed seed vectors.
- Step 3, residual: K_p = rownormalize(B_p + W_o H), with W_o zero-initialised. At initialisation K_p equals the baseline, and learning can only add a correction.
- Properties: permutation-invariant over children, works for any fanout, about 0.1M parameters.
- Recursion: a level-2 node aggregates the K rows of its children (a set of f*m vectors), so the same module compresses descendants level by level.
- Outputs: K_p (routing) and z_p (state).

4. Lateral scorer L_phi.
- Input: [z_u * z_v (elementwise), |z_u - z_v|, a time-gap bucket embedding, number of shared entities, a same-parent flag, the level pair].
- A 2-layer MLP (256 hidden) outputs w_uv in (0,1) and type logits {topic, entity, temporal sequel, update/contradiction}.
- Candidate pairs come only from the top-8 key neighbours, shared entities and time adjacency, so it runs at most 8 times per write. About 0.2M parameters.
- Used for personalised PageRank expansion at read time and as a merge feature.

5. Op policy pi_psi, the "small reasoning model between nodes". A small MLP over local site features, with two heads.
- Insert head, once per new leaf. Features of the top-3 candidate parents: placement score, margin to the next candidate, time gap to the parent's last child, fanout, level, gist staleness, entity overlap. Output: a softmax over {attach c1, attach c2, attach c3, open a new sibling under parent(c1), default = the current session node}.
- Maintenance head, once per site when the phone is idle. Features: max key cosine to the nearest sibling, child dispersion (mean pairwise child cosine), fanout, heap residual rho_p, age, access count, staleness. Output: {no-op, merge with nearest sibling, 2-way split, collapse into parent, archive (soft forget)}.
- Hard masks: fanout in [4, 32], depth at most 5, never cross a privacy boundary.
- At inference it takes the deterministic argmax (ties by id), so any behaviour can be replayed exactly. About 50k parameters.
- Hard deletion is never a policy action.

6. Gist writer (writes text; not part of the embedding layer).
- An on-device LLM writes G_p from the children's text: Apple Foundation Models today, a small open model later. Claude writes teacher gists only for public or synthetic training data.
- Its output enters the vector layer only through g_p = E(G_p), so a better or worse writer never invalidates the learned weights.
- The small LLM may also be asked to confirm a high-impact merge (more than 64 leaves). That is a rare, logged, undoable check, not the decision maker.

Why not a small LLM at every node: the cost on a phone at every write, and non-determinism, which would break replay and deletion equivalence. The small shared nets make the continuous decisions; the LLM writes the text and acts as a teacher at training time.
result.dynamic_ops:
RULE FOR EVERY OP
- Change the stored truth (text, child lists, edges).
- Recompute the Merkle hashes on the path to the root.
- Lazily recompute any derived vector whose (H, v) key is missing.
- Append to the op log: op type; inputs and outputs as ids plus hashes; weight version v; policy features and logits; the inverse op. Derived vectors are never logged, because they can always be recomputed.

Cost assumptions: d = 384, fanout f at most 32, m at most 8, depth L at most 5. One aggregator call is about 3 to 5 M multiply-adds (MAC), well under a millisecond on the phone's CPU or Neural Engine. One leaf encoder pass is about 5 to 15 ms.

CREATE LEAF
- x = E(t), a = A(x): one encoder pass. Add BM25 postings.
- Placement: route P(x) down the tree as in the read path, O(L*B*f*m*d), about 1M MAC. The policy's insert head decides.
- Recompute K and z for the at most L ancestors (about L aggregator calls). Score at most 8 lateral candidates.
- Total about 10 to 20 ms.
- The parent's gist is NOT regenerated now. Its staleness counter goes up, and the aggregator (trained with stale or absent gists) keeps routing correct. Gists are regenerated in batches once more than 25% of a node's children are new, or overnight while charging.

MERGE(p, q) into r
- children(r) = children(p) plus children(q). One aggregator call for r, plus L for the ancestors.
- Lateral edges: union, deduplicated, re-scored.
- The gist is queued for regeneration; in the meantime the two gists are concatenated.
- p and q become undo tombstones, keeping their gists for the undo window. Inverse: split r back into the logged partition.

SPLIT(p) into p1, p2
- Partition by 2-means on the child keys, seeded deterministically with the two farthest children, or use the policy's proposal.
- 2 + L aggregator calls.
- Edges move to whichever half holds their support leaves; the support sets make this exact. Inverse: merge.

COLLAPSE(p)
- The children attach to parent(p): 1 + (L - 1) aggregator calls. Inverse: re-insert p with its logged child list.

REWRITE
- Gist rewrite (corrected or regenerated): g_p = E(G_p'), one encoder pass plus L aggregator calls.
- Leaf rewrite (a user correction): a new leaf version in the same slot. The old version stays in version history unless the edit is a privacy edit.

FORGET, SOFT (archive; a policy action)
- The leaf leaves the active child set (path recompute). Its text moves to a cold store that the read path does not scan. Undoable.

FORGET, HARD (privacy deletion; started by the user or a rule, never by the policy; not undoable)
1. Purge t_i, x_i, a_i, the BM25 postings, any cite, usage and query-log rows that reference i, undo tombstones, and cache entries keyed by H_i.
2. Remove i from every edge's support set. Delete edges whose support is now empty; re-score the rest.
3. Quarantine every ancestor whose gist provenance includes i (it is not served). Regenerate its gist FROM SCRATCH from the remaining children, never by editing, so no paraphrase survives. A leak check then verifies that no rare token or entity unique to i appears in the new gist.
4. Delete ancestors left with 0 children; collapse ancestors left with 1.
5. Rewrite the op-log rows to drop the content and also the hash of i, because short text hashes can be brute-forced.
6. Optional exact structural unlearning: replay the deterministic policy over the op log of the smallest affected subtree, without event i. This removes the influence i had on where later items were placed. Cost: O(subtree events) policy calls plus gist regeneration for the nodes that changed.
7. SQLite secure_delete plus incremental vacuum.
- Guarantee: after the deletion, every derived vector equals a from-scratch build without i, given the same structure, and with replay also the same structure.
- The global weights never trained on private data, so they hold nothing about i and need no unlearning.

WEIGHT UPDATE (a new bundle v' ships with an app update)
- Leaf x vectors do not change, because the encoder is frozen. So there is none of the REALM/Atlas re-embedding cost.
- Recompute a for all N leaves (about 25k MAC each), then K, z and w bottom-up for all internal nodes (about N/8 aggregator calls). For N = 100,000 that is about 40 billion MAC: seconds to a minute in a background task.
- Build this as a shadow index under v'. Run a label-free canary on the device: beam-vs-flat agreement and heap residual on probe queries. These are metrics only and never leave the device. Then swap atomically, and keep v for rollback.
- The existing structure is NOT rebuilt by the new policy, so it stays stable and inspectable. The new policy acts only on new events and maintenance. theta is trained to be robust to trees built by older policies.

ENCODER MIGRATION (rare, e.g. bge-small to a successor)
- Re-embed all leaves and gists: about 100,000 x 10 ms, roughly 17 minutes while charging.
- Keep a dual index until it finishes. Retrain all heads offline against the new encoder and ship them as a new bundle.

UNDO (any non-privacy op)
- Apply the logged inverse to the stored truth. The vectors follow automatically through the hashes.
result.training:
PRINCIPLE
- The graph is the INPUT to a small shared network, never its parameters.
- Every loss is computed on a snapshot (content, structure). In the forward pass every derived vector is recomputed from the frozen leaf embeddings with the current weights. That is cheap: about 6k leaves x 25k MAC, plus a few hundred aggregator calls per LoCoMo conversation.
- So training never reads a stale embedding. Contrast REALM and Atlas, where a trained document encoder forces asynchronous re-indexing.
- There is no backprop through structural choices.
- There is no BPTT across events, because node state is a function of the current child set, not a recurrent memory as in TGN.
- The only temporal credit-assignment problem left is the discrete op policy. It is handled with search-based counterfactuals (Stage C).

DATA (never private)
- LoCoMo training conversations. The held-out conversations stay untouched for testing.
- Public multi-session dialogue (MSC).
- Synthetic multi-month and multi-year persona streams generated by Claude. They contain planted facts, updates, contradictions, cross-session multi-hop facts, timed questions with evidence ids, privacy-deletion requests, and simulated reasoning-plane cites with controlled noise (0 to 60% wrong).
- LongMemEval-style sets are for evaluation only.
- An EPISODE = an event stream e_1..e_T, plus timed queries (q, t_q, evidence set), plus timed deletions.
- Claude writes teacher gists for these public and synthetic texts; they are cached by child-set hash. Cheap extractive gists (the 3 most central children) stand in for counterfactual structures.

STAGE A: LEAF BRIDGES (already exist)
- Bidirectional InfoNCE: L_A = -log softmax_i(<s(q), a_e> / tau_A) - log softmax_q(<a_e, s(q)> / tau_A), rank 16.
- Then freeze A and S, or keep EMA copies A-bar and S-bar if they are co-trained later, so that Stage B's targets are stationary.

STAGE B: STRUCTURE-ROBUST AGGREGATOR AND LATERAL SCORER (supervised plus self-distillation)
- Structure distribution D_S, sampled per training conversation:
  - natural (turn to session to 4-session block);
  - time buckets;
  - agglomerative or k-means topic trees on the a vectors;
  - perturbed trees (30% random merges, splits, moves and collapses);
  - trees built by the current and past op policies (a replay buffer).
  Fanout and depth are sampled within the masks.
- Gist augmentation: teacher gist 50%, absent 30%, stale gist 10% (from a version where 10 to 30% of the children differ), extractive 10%.
- Max-heap target (label-free and exact): t(q,p) = tau * log sum over i in leaves(p) of exp(<s-bar(q), a-bar_i> / tau). This is the soft max of flat retrieval over p's subtree. A pseudo-query never counts its own source leaf.
- L_heap = sum over levels l, sum over sibling sets G at level l, of KL( softmax_{p in G}(t(q,p)/T) || softmax_{p in G}(r_theta(q,p)/T) ), plus 0.1 * mean_p (r_theta(q,p) - t(q,p))^2.
  - The listwise KL term matches what beam search actually uses: the relative order among siblings.
  - The MSE term keeps scores calibrated across levels.
